precepts.text: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, and to seeds, as of many; but as of one: and to thy seed, which is Christ. Through that chosen lineage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob came the twelve tribes and came Jesus the Christ. The law was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made. As soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with. The promise by faith of Jesus Christ is given to them that believe: it is not talking about everybody, it is the Israelites that believe on Christ that get the promises.
precepts.point: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above. If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is now what you do. But if you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you. All Israel is not Israel, as it says in Romans 9:6.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above.” If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is what you do. If you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you; all Israel is not Israel, as Romans 9:6 says. Galatians shows who it is for.

“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made.” Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and from that came the twelve tribes of Israel. “He saith not, And to seeds, as of many”: not to every nation, just that chosen lineage. “But as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.” Through that lineage came Jesus the Christ.

“Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made.” The promise was made to the twelve tribes of Israel. As soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with. “Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.”

“Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid.” If a law could have given life, righteousness would have been by the law. “But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.” That is not talking about everybody. From verse 16 it is the Israelites that believe on Christ who get the promises. There should be no confusion: those are the ones risen with Christ.

precepts.text: Even with all of that, the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham. The Lord already knew we were going to become heathens, and he saw it beforehand. We are still God's chosen people.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Our enemies would like to think God cast us away because we became like the heathen, and that he isn't going to redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

The scripture foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us, and he would justify us through faith, through Christ. They may be mad all over again; it doesn't matter. We are still God's chosen people.

So the heathen Galatians speaks of justifying is Israel fallen into heathenism, the same servants Colossians 3:22 speaks to. That justification is only for one people, as Isaiah 45:25 shows.

precepts.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. The Greek-speaking Jews and the Jews, the Israelite servant and the Israelite master, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman: we are all one nation under Christ. That is all it is talking about.
precepts.point: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal. They claimed they were the masters; did they do that? No. They lived in the big house while we lived in the outhouse, and we never got the forty acres and the mule. So they showed themselves hypocrites and impostors. The verse ends: knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Now this makes more sense: “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.”

Neither Jew nor Greek we already understand from Colossians 3:11: the Greek-speaking Jews and the Jews. Neither bond nor free: the Israelite servant and the Israelite master. Neither male nor female: the manservant and the maidservant, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman.

“for ye are all one”: we are all one nation, under Christ. That is all it is talking about. So the servants and masters of Colossians 4:1 are one people in Christ, and that is why the master must give the servant what is just and equal.

precepts.text: Cursed be he that maketh a graven image, dishonours his parents, removes the landmark, lies with a beast or his sister, takes reward to slay the innocent, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law; all the people said amen. Moral law, loving thy neighbour, agreed to on pain of death, and that is where Galatians 3:10 quotes from.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Galatians 3:10 says, “For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” Deuteronomy 27 is where Paul is quoting from.

“Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” That is death, and we agreed to it: break these commandments and we would be destroyed. Then it goes down the list. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”, that is, dishonours them. Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow, that lieth with his father's wife. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast”: no animal atones for that. Cursed be he that lieth with his sister or his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that “taketh reward to slay an innocent person.” And every time, all the people said Amen. They agreed to being cursed if they violated these laws.

Then the last: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” That is the line Paul quotes. All these things go into morality, civil and moral law, dealing with your brother, your father, your sister; it goes right back to loving thy neighbour as thyself.

That is the curse. Idolatry, adultery, murder, bestiality: there was no repentance and no animal in the temple that could atone for them. The Galatians, the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites, were heavily rooted in idolatry, so under the old covenant they were immediately condemned. That is why Paul asks whether they received the Spirit by the works of the law. If you are under that law of sacrifice, you are under the curse, because what you are guilty of cannot be atoned for under Mosaic law. They came into the faith hearing that Christ had died for them and redeemed them from sins the animals could never cover.

precepts.text: His soul which is lifted up is not upright in him, that is Esau; but the just shall live by his faith, which Paul quotes, and the just are those keeping the law, holy, just and good.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Galatians 3:11 says, “But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” The law that cannot justify is the law of sacrifice. Paul is quoting Habakkuk 2:4.

“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. That is Esau. His soul is not right by spirit, by nature, by biology; that nation is not right at all in the spirit or in their heads. “but the just shall live by his faith.” That is where Paul got it.

Abraham's faith was counted for righteousness, and his faith came first, before his works; then his works proved his faith, because they go hand in hand. So the just shall live by faith, and that faith is faith in Christ. The just are those keeping God's laws, the law that is holy, just and good, and they live by faith in Christ, not by the blood of animals.

precepts.text: The law is holy and the commandment holy, just and good: what makes you just, and the just live by faith in Christ.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
What makes you just, so that you live by faith? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

So when you are just, what are you keeping? God's laws. And what will you live by? Faith in Christ. That is what Habakkuk is talking about when he says the just shall live by his faith, and that is what Paul is talking about in Galatians 3:11. The just are those who keep God's commandments, and they shall live by faith.

So Paul is not throwing away the commandments. The law that cannot justify is the law of sacrifice; the commandments are what make a man just, and the just man lives by faith in Christ.

precepts.text: Caiaphas: it is expedient that one man die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Both kingdoms were condemned under the covenant they kept violating, and that is the curse of the law Christ died to take us out of.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Caiaphas points out what the curse of the law is. “And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.”

Why would the whole nation perish? Because they were under the old covenant that they agreed to and kept violating over and over again. The northern kingdom went off first, and the southern kingdom fell right after, and both were destroyed by the nations. Standing in the old covenant, based on our own actions and on the law and the prophets, both kingdoms were condemned. By default both were under the curse of the law, which is condemnation. They should have been destroyed.

But the Lord had other plans. He said, I will not destroy them; I love them; I am going to have my son go and die for them, and redeem them from the curse they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27, where all the people said Amen. That is Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse and death are the same thing; being made a curse for us means he was killed for us. Christ died to take us out of that contract and put us into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, the northern kingdom.

precepts.text: What the law could not do in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending his Son and condemned sin in the flesh: he ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by his death.
precepts.point: Ye who were kept under the law are all the children of God by faith in Christ, whether Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female, the same people in different conditions. If ye be Christ's then are ye Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise, and the promise pertains to Israel; name me one other nation God calls his people in the Old Testament.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” The we is Israel, kept under the law of sacrifice until Christ came on the scene and died for us, the same as Hebrews 9 saying it was imposed until the time of reformation. “Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”: our mentor, our stepping stone, the placeholder for Christ's body being offered in the end. “that we might be justified by faith”: Christ's death justifies us, not the law of sacrifice.

What was it that could not justify? “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”. The law referred to here is animal sacrifice. Weak through the flesh means through our flesh, and it involves the animals as well. “God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”.

He did away with our condemnation by his own death. As Caiaphas said, it is expedient that one man should die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Christ ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by dying on the cross.

So “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Christ has come and gone, and we are all the children of God by faith in Christ, not by animal sacrifice. That was the bewitching earlier in the chapter: that you could be justified without Christ, and all you needed was an animal.

precepts.text: A disannulling of the commandment for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof, for the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope, Christ, did: the annulled commandment is sacrifice.
precepts.point: Ye who were kept under the law are all the children of God by faith in Christ, whether Jew or Greek, bond or free, male or female, the same people in different conditions. If ye be Christ's then are ye Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise, and the promise pertains to Israel; name me one other nation God calls his people in the Old Testament.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” What commandment was annulled? Sacrifice. It was annulled for its weakness and unprofitableness, done away in Christ. That is the same weakness as Romans 8:3, the law that was weak through the flesh.

“For the law made nothing perfect”. What law made nothing perfect? Hebrews 10:1 said the sacrifices offered could not make the comers thereunto perfect. It made no man perfect. “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” Not what, but who: Christ is the better hope, and through him we draw nigh unto God.

That is why “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”. The schoolmaster, the law of sacrifice, was disannulled, and the ye who were kept under it, whether called Jews or Greeks, bond or free, male or female, are the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The promise pertains to the Israelites. All nations are not the children of promise. If they are, name the nation God calls his people in the old covenant. Isaiah 19 says Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands, but Isaiah 27, Isaiah 11 and Zechariah 10 show that means the children of Israel gathered out of Egypt and Assyria. That is called precepts.

precepts.text: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.
precepts.point: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James says “the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.” Paul quotes the same scripture to the Galatians: “Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”

Abraham’s belief was accounted for righteousness, and James shows how it was fulfilled: when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” Faith worked together with his actions, and his actions perfected it.

“Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.” Rahab the harlot was justified the same way. She believed that if she helped the spies escape, they would spare her life; that was her faith, and receiving the messengers and sending them out another way was her works. “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” We have to keep the commandments and the faith of Christ; each goes with the other.

precepts.text: Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, and in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities. The blessing on all kindreds of the earth is Christ dying for the Israelites scattered in every nation, whose blood covers us wherever we are found, since we cannot reach all our people on this earth.
precepts.point: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.” The heathen are the Gentiles: the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, justified through faith. But Christians say, see, brother, all nations will be blessed. So what does it mean?

Peter answers: “Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.” They foretold, as Paul says the scripture foresaw. “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers”. The ye are the Israelites. Abraham was a prophet, and the covenant passed from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob, “saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Unto you first, the Israelites. The blessing is Christ dying for the Israelites, for all of us scattered among all the nations. The earth is too big for us to reach all our people, but Christ's blood covers us wherever we are found. That is how all the kindreds of the earth are blessed: Israel scattered among those nations and blessed with the death of Christ.

And Esau? He already got his blessing: blood and death, slavery, weaponry, war, bloodshed, nukes and witchcraft. He is literally dropping those blessings on Iran right now. He does not need any more. The other nations' blessing is to work, to build up our kingdom, and to survive the destruction as servants. “So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.text: In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory. Whether called Jews or Gentiles, all the seed of Israel is justified by faith in Christ. Show me one precept where all the seed of Edom, Moab, Ishmael, or Canaan is justified; it is nowhere in the law and prophets.
precepts.point: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith”. How do we know who is justified? You will not find anywhere in the law and the prophets that Christ was going to justify, atone for or reconcile all the heathen Gentile nations through his death. What you find is this: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

All the seed of Israel, all the families scattered abroad over the earth, justified by faith in Christ. Whether they are called Jews or called Gentiles, they shall be justified, because Christ died for them among the nations.

Now show me a precept where all the seed of Edom will be justified. All the seed of Moab justified. All the seed of Ishmael, all the seed of the Canaanites. Show me one place. It is nowhere in there.

So “they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham”: the Israelites who have faith in Christ are the children of Abraham, known for his strong faith. Abraham believed God first, and only afterward offered sacrifices, and his faith, not the animal, was counted for righteousness. That is how the seed of Israel is justified, and why “they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that maketh any graven image, that setteth light by his father or mother, that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, that lieth with his father's wife, with any manner of beast, with his sister, with his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that taketh reward to slay an innocent person, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them; and all the people shall say, Amen. We all agreed, and none of these can be atoned with an animal: it is death all throughout. The white man removed the landmarks of America, Africa, and Australia and cannot atone while he sits on the stolen land.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse.” The works of the law, in Galatians 3:2, 3:5, 3:10 and 2:16, is sacrifice, as in Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. And “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them” is Paul quoting Deuteronomy 27.

What does that curse mean? “Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image”, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” Can he atone for it, reconcile with God, find justification? What animal can he use? None. Under the old covenant you get death. That is what cursed means.

So it goes all the way down. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”: disrespects, curses or strikes them. “Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark.” The so-called white man has removed the neighbor's landmark: America is a stolen landmark, Africa is a stolen landmark, Australia is a stolen landmark. How can he atone when the land is still in his possession? He can't; he sits on stolen land. “Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife”, his stepmother. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.” “Cursed be he that lieth with his sister”, “with his mother in law.” “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly”: kills his brother secretly and does not get caught. “Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person”: a hitman, a mercenary.

After each one, “all the people shall say, Amen”: we all agreed to it. Then “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them”, which is exactly what Paul quotes. None of these could be atoned for with an animal. It is death all throughout.

That is why those of the works of the law are under the curse. We confirmed to do everything under that covenant of sacrifices, and if you violate a law that no animal can cover, you get the curse, which is death.

precepts.text: Through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins, and by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. Animals could not atone for all things; Christ's death does. That is the difference.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” Justified by the law here is the same law as the works of the law in verses 2, 5 and 10 and in Galatians 2:16: the law of sacrifice.

Paul preached the same thing in Acts 13: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, and all that believe in Christ's death are justified from all things, all sins.

Could you receive justification from all things under Moses? No, because animals do not atone for all things. Does Christ's death atone for all things, reconcile us from all things, justify us from all things? Yes. That is the difference.

And the law is not of faith because faith came first. “The man that doeth them shall live in them”: the man who does the sacrifices lives until he commits a sin worthy of death, and then he cannot live anymore. The just live by faith in the one whose death covers what no animal could.

precepts.text: Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said it is expedient that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not, and prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation, and not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. The curse of the law is death on the whole nation; Christ took it on himself for Judah and for Israel scattered abroad, the ones Paul went to among the Gentiles.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.” Some people read right past that. What is the curse of the law? Death. But you need a scripture to back up what you say, and John 11 is it.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation, all twelve tribes, perishing: that is the curse of the law. All twelve tribes broke the first covenant, and by that default we were all worthy of death. When Christ died, he took that curse upon himself for us. That is “being made a curse for us”: dying for us.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only.” Not for Judah only, “but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Gather together in one is reconciliation, at-one-ment, atonement.

So Christ died for Judah and for Israel, all twelve tribes. Those scattered abroad are the ones Paul was going to among the heathen, among the Gentiles, while being called Gentiles themselves. That is how “the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”

precepts.text: If a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and thou hang him on a tree, his body shall not remain all night upon the tree, for he that is hanged is accursed of God. Hanging was our capital punishment, and Christ took on the curse, the consequence of violating the covenant, when he was hung. Acts 5:30 and Acts 10:39: whom they slew and hanged on a tree, Peter says twice.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. That is written in Deuteronomy 21: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled.” Hanging was capital punishment among us.

So Christ took on the curses for us, the punishment and consequence of violating that covenant, when he was hung. Some say he wasn't hung, he was nailed to a cross. But if you are nailed to a wooden pole, you are hanging by your hands and feet. That is a lynching. He was hung for hours.

Peter calls it the same thing, twice: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” And again, “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.” They hung Christ on a tree, on wood, a cross. Christ died a black man's death.

Do you think the lynchings among our people were a coincidence, when the white man hung us from trees and lamps and bridges? People have been hung from time to time, but not to the capacity we have been hung; it was enforced all around among us. The curse of the tree came on our people, and Christ bore that same curse to redeem us from it, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”

precepts.text: A figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices that could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience, because sin was in us since Adam; which stood only in meats and drinks, meat and drink offerings, and divers washings, baptisms, and carnal ordinances, traditions of the Pharisees, imposed until the time of reformation, when Christ came. This is an example of the works of the law.
precepts.point: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 9:3-5: Paul's kinsmen according to the flesh, Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises, whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came. The heirs are Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” Who was kept under the law? “Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law”. We were locked into that covenant until Christ came, died, and granted us liberty.

What was it we were kept under? Hebrews gives an example of the works of the law: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrifices could not make him that did them perfect, because sin was already in us since Adam. So the animals had to be temporary.

“Which stood only in meats and drinks”: meat offerings and drink offerings. These are the works of the law read all through Galatians, in 2:16, 3:2, 3:5 and 3:10-11. “and divers washings”: baptisms. “and carnal ordinances”: the traditions of the Pharisees. “imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Forced upon them until the time of reformation, which is the faith that should afterwards be revealed, when Christ came and did away with all of it.

So “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”. The schoolmaster was sacrifice. The sacrificing of animals was a foreshadowing of Christ's death, preparing us for his body. It was temporary, because we grew weary and rebellious behind it and would all have been condemned through it. “But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”: no longer under the law of sacrifice.

precepts.text: The king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers and not to live after the laws of God; neither was it lawful to keep Sabbath days or ancient feasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew. Your law, your culture, and your race go together: deny your laws and you deny your race and your God. Under that order we became Greeks, Gentiles.
precepts.point: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 9:3-5: Paul's kinsmen according to the flesh, Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises, whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came. The heirs are Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“There is neither Jew nor Greek”. Christians read it like a soft effeminate man, neither Jew nor Greek, brother, and say it means anybody. The people of Christianity have no idea about history. Why does Paul reference Greeks?

“Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God”. Your law, your culture and your race go hand in hand with God. The Bible says love your neighbour as yourself; that is law. Deny your race and you deny your laws; deny your law and you deny your God.

“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” It was basically illegal under the order of the king to call yourself a Jew or keep Jewish customs. So over time we became Greeks, Gentiles.

That is who Paul is writing to. The ye that were kept under the law in verse 23 are the same ye called Jews and Greeks, bond and free, male and female. Do not escape that context. Whatever your title or status in that present world, Jew or Greek, free like Paul or bond like others, “ye are all one in Christ Jesus”: all God's chosen people.

precepts.text: When Antiochus Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest, promising the king three hundred and threescore talents of silver and eighty more, and a hundred and fifty more if he might set him up a place for exercise, a gym, for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians. A wicked Israelite who took a Greek name, bribed the white man to remove his righteous brother, and Greekified the youth. When a man seeks leadership, he usually is not meant to lead.
precepts.point: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 9:3-5: Paul's kinsmen according to the flesh, Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises, whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came. The heirs are Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
How did Israelites become Greeks? “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest”. Jason was a wicked Israelite who changed his name to Jason, a Greek name. He sought underhandedly to be high priest against his brother Onias, a righteous man, using money to gain authority and leadership. When a man seeks leadership, he usually is not meant to be a leader at all.

“Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents”. He bribed the king of the Greeks, the white man, to force his brother out of position and put him in. “Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise”, a gym, “and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen”: training the Israelite youth in the culture of the Greeks.

“and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” He registered the Israelites of Jerusalem as citizens of Antioch, the Antioch in Turkey that Paul writes about. Becoming Antiochians was a betrayal of the ancestral laws and a shift to the Greek way of life, and that cultural tension triggered the Maccabean revolt. Antiochian and Greek are the same.

So when Paul says “There is neither Jew nor Greek”, he is writing to the descendants of those same people. Whether called Jew or Greek, “if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The heirs are Israelites, to whom pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law and the promises.

precepts.text: Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. Christ was lynched, hanged on a tree, under the same curse as his people.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.text: He that is hanged is accursed of God.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. Christ was lynched, hanged on a tree, under the same curse as his people.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Hanging was our punishment too, in the law, for the wicked: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:” “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”.

That is what Paul quotes in Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. The curse of the law means its condemnation; being made a curse means being put to death for us, a sacrifice.

So what happened to our people? We were hanged on trees, because we went under the curses. Christ went under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us, and we are under the curses too. He that is hanged is accursed of God: Christ was hanged on a tree, and so were we. The King and his children were hanged.

And the pattern keeps turning, like a ring. In Egypt, when Moses said, let my people go to serve God, Pharaoh called us idle and took away the straw but kept the tale of bricks, with a quota of 2,000 bricks; the records name Yupa son of Uriah, a Hebrew, 370 short. Here it was a quota of 200 or 500 pounds of cotton. The officers set over us, the black elites, pastors and politicians in the white man's pocket, turned on Moses and Aaron for making Pharaoh hate them. It is the same curse, the same judgment, until Christ, who bore the curse, redeems us from it.

precepts.text: The covenant that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law: so covenant, law and wisdom are all the same thing.
precepts.point: So wisdom and the commandments are interchangeable, and it is the statutes the nations hear that make us a wise and understanding people.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, neither bond nor free, for ye are all one in Christ Jesus; look at the auction blocks and the zoos and tell me that was ever taught about us in the white man's church.
precepts.point: Those verses only began to be preached about black and brown people once the civil rights movement started, and that is why the churches will not look at these images; the pictures contradict what they say John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 mean.

note.label: The Fallacy of Black Christians

precepts.text: Received ye the spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? So the question is what the works of the law are.
precepts.point: Never let a Christian confound you in these verses. They do not know the Bible; we do.

note.label: The Fallacy of Black Christians

precepts.text: The promise was to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ.
precepts.point: The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

note.label: Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines

precepts.why:
“In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.” That seed is not a crowd; it is one. “Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.”

The oath sworn to Abraham and performed unto Isaac is a promise about Christ. So in thy seed shall all nations be blessed does not put everybody in the covenant. The blessing comes through Christ, and through Christ scattered Israel in all kindreds of the earth receives repentance and comes back to the Father.

precepts.text: As many as are of the works of the law are under the curse without continuing in all things written.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.

note.label: Jeremiah 11: The Broken Covenant

precepts.why:
Paul repeats the same curse: “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” The curse Jeremiah was sent to proclaim did not pass away with the prophets; it is written in the New Testament word for word.

“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse”. It is not enough to start in the law; the man that does not continue in all things written in the book is under the curse. That is the man Jeremiah 11:3 is speaking of, the man that obeys not the words of this covenant.

precepts.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, so Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy while the other nations must go through them.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.”

We are the ones redeemed from the curse; Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy, while the other nations must go through them. That is why Jeremiah could pray, “Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them. Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” The Most High pleaded the causes of his soul and redeemed his life, and we will see our enemies go through the curse for eternity while we reign forever.

precepts.text: The promises were made "to Abraham and his seed... not... to seeds, as of many; but as of one... which is Christ," so the blessing comes through the one seed, Christ, to the same people.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.”

The promises were made to Abraham and his seed, and the seed through which the blessing comes is one, Christ. The blessing to the kindreds of the earth comes through that one seed to the same people, the children of the covenant Peter is speaking to.

precepts.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.” That is the one “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.”

“That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.” The Gentiles here are the northern tribes. Christ redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on them.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: This is what they do. “There is neither Jew nor Greek,” They say, see, everybody is in. Listen: there is neither Jew nor Greek, why? Because they are one race of people. The Greeks Paul went to were the Jews who were forbidden to call themselves Jews and were forced to eat Greek, speak Greek, dress Greek, worship Greek. Paul had to undo all that madness that our people were in. “there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” So what is Paul talking about? Unity. He is unifying the nation of Israel once again at that time. It is the same mission that we are on today, the same mission.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

precepts.why: A side note; this came up in Uganda, when a Christian challenged us. “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law”: the curse is Deuteronomy 28:15 down. The brother asked, if Christ redeemed us from the curse, why are we still oppressed? Go back to Luke 21:22: “that all things which are written may be fulfilled.” Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil, so everything Moses prophesied must happen to the children of Israel. Yes, he redeemed us from the curse, but there is a time period; everything must come to pass. The slave ship just happened, and now you can see the curses starting to be lifted off of us.

points: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth? Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are ye so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh of animals? Have ye suffered so many things in vain? He that worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law? Verses 2 and 5 are the same sacrifice as 2:16.

God promised him a son and land and seed as the sand of the sea, Abraham believed, and only afterward offered sacrifices; his faith came first and that was counted for righteousness, not the animal. They which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse, for it is written, cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. Works of the law in verses 2, 5, and 10 and in 2:16 is sacrifice, Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: No man is justified by the law in the sight of God, for the just shall live by faith. The law is not of faith, because faith came first; but the man that doeth them shall live in them, until he commits a sin worthy of death. Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, dying for us; the curse of the law is death, which all twelve tribes earned by breaking the first covenant.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: The covenant that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. Abraham's promise predates the Mosaic and sacrificial law. If the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise, but God gave it to Abraham by promise, and the promise comes first.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, the sin within us, to keep us in check, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made, and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator, Moses. Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid; if there had been a law which could have given life, righteousness should have been by the law, but there is none because man is sinful by nature.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: The scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. All nations are sinful, but not all are under sin. Romans 3:9: we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin. Romans 11:26-32: all Israel shall be saved, for God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all; the all under sin and in unbelief is all Israel.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Who was under the law? Romans 3:19: what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law. Locked into that covenant until Christ came and granted us liberty.
